title: Sharada Tilaka Tantra (Laxmanacharya)
shelf_note: Śāradātilaka of Lakṣmaṇadeśika, a core Śākta/mantraśāstra manual; belongs on the Hindu Sanskrit shelf.
structure_note: printed_backsteps 59 and printed_repeats 69 out of 286 numbered pages are high. In this sample the OCR misread the printed numerals: page 222 is printed २१९ but stored as 214, and page 150 is printed १४७ but stored as 149. That points to numeral misreads, not misordered leaves. No duplicates; all 291 pages have OCR and a translation.

reader_summary: This is a plain-text printed edition of the Śāradātilaka, and the transcription is of the right text. Ritual verses come through readably. The mantroddhāra passages, where single syllables matter, are misread, and the English then invents syllables and results ('makes the invisible visible'). Verse numbers and chapter headings sometimes drift. Do not use the English for any mantra or prayoga without checking the Sanskrit.
book_verdict: Right text, readable OCR with frequent small misreads. The English is good enough for the ritual narrative but unreliable on mantra syllables and stated rite outcomes, and it adds headings and verse numbers in the wrong places.

title: Tantraloka Vol. 1 with Jayaratha Commentary
shelf_note: KSTS edition of Abhinavagupta's Tantrāloka with Jayaratha's Viveka; central to the Kashmir Śaiva shelf.
structure_note: Pages 51, 182 and 211 are in the first āhnika, printed 41, 172 and 201 (a steady offset of 10). Page 348, however, is printed 26 under the running head श्रीतन्त्रालोकः, and its verse 32 cites the Triśirobhairava. That looks like the opening of the next KSTS volume (āhnika 2) bound into or appended to this scan. If so, the 'Vol. 1' title undersells the content, and the restart of printed numbering explains part of the 28 backsteps and 73 repeats. pages_translated_field (359) disagrees with the counted 368.

tr_errors.problem: A carried-over fragment '...ed.' opens the page; the gloss of a word split across the page boundary (…vikalpavṛttīnām) is inferred

reader_summary: This is the KSTS Tantrāloka with Jayaratha's commentary, transcribed accurately, footnoted variants included, from a clean 1918 print. The English is careful and close to the commentary, with occasional unbracketed glosses and fragments carried across page breaks. The scan appears to run on into the next volume's second āhnika.
book_verdict: Sound transcription and a trustworthy, slightly expansive translation. The caveats are a page-seam fragment and a scan that seems to include part of the following volume under a 'Vol. 1' title.

title: Paramesvaratantra
shelf_note: Cambridge palm-leaf manuscript of the Parameśvaratantra (dated 828/9 CE, early Nepalese script); a key early Śaiva source.
structure_note: The leaves carry modern foliation in the left margin (31 on page 62, 40 on page 80, 56 on page 112), consistent with two images per leaf. The OCR's page numbers do not match these: it gives 3 for leaf 31 and 41 for leaf 40. Only 52 of 124 pages have a printed number, so the backstep and repeat counts measure the OCR's inventions, not the order of the leaves.

reader_summary: The images are the Cambridge palm leaves of the Parameśvaratantra, one of the oldest dated Sanskrit manuscripts, and they are good to look at. The transcription is mostly not this text: the engine cannot read the early Nepalese script and fills the lines with plausible or non-Sanskrit words. The English then turns those words into fluent mantras and narratives, so none of the text can be trusted.
book_verdict: Valuable manuscript images under an OCR that is largely confabulated and an English that elaborates it. It should not be shown as a reading text, and it needs a reader of the script.

title: Rig-Veda-Sanhita: Sacred Hymns of the Brahmans (Vol. 3)
shelf_note: Max Müller's editio princeps of the Ṛgveda with Sāyaṇa's commentary, vol. 3 (maṇḍalas 5–7).
structure_note: The published date of 1849 belongs to vol. 1; vol. 3 appeared in 1856, a minor metadata error. Page 2 is a blank flyleaf, correctly marked blank. The backsteps (101) and repeats (134) are plausibly roman-numbered front matter and numeral misreads; the sampled body pages run in order (309, 623, 922).

reader_summary: This is Müller's Ṛgveda with Sāyaṇa (maṇḍalas 5–7). The saṃhitā, padapāṭha and commentary are transcribed accurately with accents. The English follows Sāyaṇa closely and is mostly reliable, with an occasional inverted line in the hymn rendering and added section headings.
book_verdict: A strong book: correct text, near-perfect OCR, and a careful commentary-led translation. Warn that the verse renderings are working translations and occasionally slip (7.4.7).
